correctness.rationale: For any finite abelian A, an invariant edge orbit corresponds to inversion class ±d and a collection forms a fixed-point simplex precisely if its Cayley graph admits parity character χ on generated subgroup with χ(d)=1. Odd-order direct factors can be projected away by a contiguous simplicial retraction. For cyclic 2^a, admissible nonempty sets have a common valuation k, giving a disjoint union of a simplices. For C_(2^a)×C2, cover by 2a+1 facet simplices F_k, G_(−1), G_k; all multiple intersections simplices, the G-facet nerve has a contractible core, and a extra edges F_kG_k each produce one S¹. Independent BFS Cayley enumeration for a=1,2,3 yields reduced Euler characteristics −1,−2,−3 (and f-vectors [1,3,3],[1,5,8,2],[1,9,26,24,11,2]); proof of nerve collapse establishes integral homotopy, not just mod-two Betti numbers. Scope excludes 2-primary rank≥3.
